description: Flat vector geometry on a near-black square ground, drawn in a two-hue palette: a warm ochre/amber and a cool desaturated slate blue-grey, both used at partial opacity so overlaps darken into brown and charcoal pools. The vocabulary is a small set of hard-edged primitives -- equilateral triangles, squares/diamonds, discs and star-polygons -- repeated around a centre under rotational symmetry (3-fold, 6-fold and 12-fold instances are all present), with a secondary scatter of smaller copies of the same primitive drifting outward. Composition is almost always centred with generous margin, though two or three tokens (9548, 10980) push their outer scatter off the edge and clip. Density is the widest-swinging variable: 9190 is a dense saturated starburst and 9369/9906/10085 are single large solid discs with a dark star or eye bitten out of the middle, while 9011, 10622 and 10801 are very sparse and very dark -- a handful of low-luminance grey triangles that barely separate from the background. What the twelve share is the palette, the flat-polygon language, the centred rotational construction and the amber-on-near-black key; what differs is the governing primitive, the fold count, the scale of the central element and, most of all, brightness. Across the three condition rows the change is consistent: neutral is the baseline, stress brightens and enlarges the ochre and adds a large stroked (outline-only) figure that was not there before -- a bright amber triangle outline on 9011, an amber 12-point star outline on 9548, a bigger and more saturated star on 9190, a bigger disc on 9369 -- and recovery falls back to something very close to neutral, slightly larger and duller than the stress frame but recognisably the neutral image again.
seenAt120: The silhouette classes survive and stay separable: the solid amber disc, the diamond, the dense starburst, the big triangle outlines, the loose scatter fields, the tight cluster. Interior detail does not -- the 12-point star inside 9369's disc collapses to a scalloped edge, and the layered overlaps in 9190 flatten into one mass. Four of the twelve (9011, 10622, 10801, 10980) drop close to invisible: their grey-on-near-black triangles lose almost all contrast and read as empty or near-empty tiles, so at browse size the grid looks like roughly eight images and four blanks. Anything ochre reads immediately; anything relying on the slate grey alone mostly does not.
